gold_label: Plausible disease-relevant target; toxic-species definition, target engagement, and CNS exposure are key uncertainties
gold_rationale: Alpha-synuclein aggregation is central to Lewy pathology, so small-molecule aggregation inhibition is mechanistically relevant. The major uncertainties are which conformer/oligomer is pathogenic, how to demonstrate in vivo target engagement, and achieving CNS exposure; clinical disease modification is unproven.
red_flags: claims aggregation inhibition is proven disease-modifying
assumes a single toxic species with no uncertainty

criteria.name: pd_mechanism_correctness
criteria.description: Correctly describes the PD mechanism linking the target to disease biology (e.g. GBA1/GCase/lysosome/alpha-synuclein, LRRK2 kinase, mitochondrial).

criteria.name: target_relevance
criteria.description: Justifies why the proposed target is therapeutically relevant to PD.

criteria.name: disease_subtype_reasoning
criteria.description: Reasons about the relevant patient subgroup / disease subtype where applicable.

criteria.name: evidence_uncertainty
criteria.description: Identifies the main mechanistic and evidentiary uncertainties.

criteria.name: overclaiming_avoidance
criteria.description: Does not claim proven clinical disease modification from mechanistic plausibility.
